kentat: ### What did I do, and how?
### Why did I do it this way?

36.otsikko: GDD into tasks, project set up

tehtavat.teksti: Read the brief and your own GDD side by side and write a question list for the client.
Scope P0 with your instructor and split it into issues, each with a done-when condition.
Set up the Unity project with the agreed version and a public GitHub repository — run the privacy check.
Name the game team, hold the first weekly meeting and put the implementation plan into project-docs.

36.nayta: a public repository whose README, P0 milestone and first commit say what is being built — plus the question list with answers and the meeting note in project-docs.
36.tuotos: A public GitHub repository, a P0 milestone with issues, a question list for the client, the GDD and the implementation plan in project-docs, and the first weekly meeting note.
36.valmis: An outsider can see from the repository what is being built and in which order: the README describes the game in one paragraph, the milestone "MVP 4 Dec" holds the P0 issues, and the project compiles as an empty scene.
36.label: 31 Aug – 4 Sep

37.otsikko: Tanks move — two players, one keyboard

tehtavat.teksti: Build the tank prefab (square body and round turret) with a Rigidbody2D and colliders.
Implement two-player movement on one keyboard: WASD and the arrow keys.
Write two test cases and number them T01 and T02: record the expected result before running them, then run them — plus the weekly meeting note.

37.nayta: a playable build with two tanks moving, test cases T01–T02 with results in tests.md, and the movement commits.
37.tuotos: A tank prefab (square body + round turret per the GDD), two-player input mapping (WASD / arrows), Rigidbody2D-based movement, a fixed test arena. 2 recorded test cases.
37.valmis: Two players can move at the same time on one keyboard without the keys interfering with each other, and the tanks stop at a wall without jittering.
37.label: 7–11 Sep

tehtavat.teksti: Build the Projectile prefab with a physics material: Bounciness 1, Friction 0.
Implement shooting: one shell per player on the field, slightly faster than the tank.
Implement a ~10 s despawn and hits — including on your own tank (friendly fire).
Write test cases T03–T05 before running them: direct hit, ricochet chain, despawn time.

38.nayta: a video or image sequence of the ricocheting shell, test cases T03–T05 with results, and the Projectile prefab commit.
38.tuotos: A Projectile prefab and shooting for both players: one shell per player on the field, ricochet through a physics material, despawn on a timer. 3 recorded test cases.
38.valmis: The shell bounces off walls without losing speed, disappears in about 10 seconds, kills its own shooter too, and a new shell can only be fired once the previous one is gone.
38.label: 14–18 Sep

39.otsikko: Rounds, scoring and the five-second rule

tehtavat.teksti: Implement tank destruction and round cleanup: shells removed, input cut from the dead tank.
Implement scoring, the GDD's five-second rule and the automatic round restart.
Write test cases T06–T08 before running them and play with the game team — note the round rhythm.

39.nayta: a whole round without the editor: scoring, the 5 s rule tested (T06–T08) and the playtest note week39.md.
39.tuotos: GameManager: tank destruction, scoring, the 5 s rule, round restart, a score display at the top of the screen — the first version of the HUD, the heads-up display drawn on top of the running match. 3 recorded test cases.
39.valmis: A whole round works without touching the editor: destruction, a point to the right player (or to neither, under the 5 s rule), and an automatic new round.
39.label: 21–25 Sep

40.otsikko: Generated maze and data out of the code

tehtavat.teksti: Write the data store comparison (ScriptableObject / JSON / PlayerPrefs) before implementing anything.
Implement the maze generator with depth-first search (DFS) as its own class — draw the algorithm on paper first.
Build the arena from data and implement spawn validation: starting positions at least 3 tiles apart.
Write test cases T09–T10 before running them: traversability and spawn distance.

40.nayta: the written data store comparison, the paper drawing of the depth-first search, generated mazes and test cases T09–T10.
40.tuotos: MazeGenerator (DFS), 10×10 working (5×5 and 25×25 as P1 issues), spawn validation, arena configuration in a ScriptableObject or JSON + a written data store comparison. 2 recorded test cases.
40.valmis: Every generated 10×10 maze is fully traversable (DFS guarantees it), the tanks start at least 3 tiles apart, and the arena size is read from data — you can change the size without touching code.
40.label: 28 Sep – 2 Oct

tehtavat.teksti: Define the power-ups as data: SpeedBoost, Slowness and Shield assets with their durations.
Implement spawning (~2 s interval, at tile centres), pickup and the one-power-at-a-time rule.
Show the active powers in the HUD and on the tank, and write test cases T11–T12 before running them.

41.nayta: three power-up assets as data, a HUD screenshot and test cases T11–T12 with results.
41.tuotos: The power-up system: spawning (~2 s interval, only into free normal tiles), pickup, one power at a time (GDD), duration timers, a HUD icon and a tank indicator. Speed +20 %/10 s, slowness −20 %/10 s on the opponent, shield 15 s or one hit. 2 recorded test cases.
41.valmis: Three powers work with their durations, a player can only hold one at a time (a new one is not picked up before the old one is spent — GDD), and a spectator can see both players' state from the HUD.
41.label: 5–9 Oct

tehtavat.teksti: Prepare a 10-minute demo of the playable build and run the review for the client.
Write the review note in two parts: the client's own words and your interpretation, kept separate.
Make the prioritisation decision with the game team and update the implementation plan and the backlog.

43.nayta: the review note in the client's words, the recorded prioritisation decision and the updated implementation plan.
43.tuotos: A review note (the client's words kept separate from your interpretation), the game team's prioritisation decision from the P1 list (laser / triple shot / special tiles / audio — the chosen one must fit roughly 2 working days), and an updated implementation plan.
43.valmis: The note holds the client's own words, your interpretation separately, and a named decision: what gets built in week 44, what moves to P1/P2. The instructor has signed off on the decision.
43.label: 19–23 Oct

44.otsikko: Feedback change and the chosen extra feature

tehtavat.teksti: Make the change derived from the feedback on its own branch and open a pull request (PR) that references the note.
Implement the feature chosen in the review, on top of the week 38 and 41 systems.
Run a game team playtest and record the shared assessment in a note.
Write test cases T13–T14 before running them and merge the pull request after review.

44.nayta: a merged PR that references the feedback, the playable feature, the playtest note and test cases T13–T14.
44.tuotos: A PR: the feedback change (branch → main) whose description references the review note; the chosen feature (e.g. triple shot) playable; the game team's playtest note with a shared assessment. 2 recorded test cases.
44.valmis: Main holds a merged PR whose description makes clear which feedback it answers; the feature works; the playtest note holds at least three shared observations and a shared assessment.
44.label: 26–30 Oct

tehtavat.teksti: Complete the test matrix from the GDD's testing list: normal, boundary and error cases in balance.
Run every test — the old ones again too — and record the result of every row.
Solve one bug with a named debugging pair and record both sets of observations.
Finish three debugging chains with all six parts.

45.nayta: the run test matrix (≥12 rows), three complete debugging chains and the pair debugging note.
45.tuotos: A run test matrix (≥12 test cases: normal / boundary / error in roughly equal thirds), 3 complete debugging chains, a debugging pair note, regression tests for the fixed bugs.
45.valmis: Every row of the matrix has an expectation recorded before the run and the result of the run; the three chains hold an observation, reproduction steps, the cause, the fix commit, a retest and a regression test; the pair note holds both names and both sets of observations.
45.label: 2–6 Nov

tehtavat.teksti: Build the main menu and the pause menu per the GDD's user interface (UI) chapter: Play, Options, Leave and resume/restart/quit.
Implement the settings and save them to PlayerPrefs — block duplicate player colours.
Write test cases T15–T16 before running them: settings persistence and the duplicate colour block.

46.nayta: the playable menu path, PlayerPrefs settings persistence (T15) and the duplicate colour block (T16).
46.tuotos: Main menu, options (arena size, player colours without duplicates; audio sliders only if audio was chosen in week 43), pause (resume / restart / quit), settings saved to PlayerPrefs. 2 recorded test cases.
46.valmis: The game can be started, the settings changed and a match paused without touching the editor; the settings are still there on the next launch; the same player colour cannot be picked twice.
46.label: 9–13 Nov

47.otsikko: Release candidate, external testing and security

tehtavat.teksti: Make the first release candidate (RC1) as build v1.0-rc1 and test it yourself in a clean folder.
Write the installation and gameplay guide: download, launch, controls, goal.
Arrange an outside tester on another machine with no spoken help, and record the findings.
Run a security review of your own repository with concrete file paths and commits.

47.nayta: the RC build, the written guide, the tester's findings in their own words and the security review with references.
47.tuotos: An RC build, an installation and gameplay guide, the outside tester's observations (name, role, date, their own words), and a security review of your own repository with concrete references.
47.valmis: The tester got all the way through a match without spoken help; every point where they hesitated is recorded as a fix list for the guide; the security review names the files and commits it checked. After the RC, only blocking bugs get fixed.
47.label: 16–20 Nov

tehtavat.teksti: Fix only the release candidate's blocking bugs and move the tester's fix list into the guide.
Publish GitHub Release v1.0 with the build files and a scope description.
Test the release in a clean environment, finish the README and LICENSE, and freeze the content.

48.nayta: GitHub Release v1.0, the clean-environment test report and the final README + LICENSE.
48.tuotos: GitHub Release v1.0 with the build files (or an itch.io release — the instructor decides), the final README, a LICENSE as agreed, a clean-environment test report, and a content freeze commit.
48.valmis: An outsider can download the release and play a match on a machine that has never had the project on it; the README matches the GDD's controls and rules; the release page states what the MVP contains and what was deliberately left out (P1/P2).
48.label: 23–27 Nov

tehtavat.teksti: Finish the project documentation so every claim has an exact reference.
Rehearse the 8–10 minute demo and time it with a game team member.
Write the self-assessment against the meeting notes and hand over the MVP on Fri 4 Dec.

49.nayta: the finished project documentation, the collected journal and AI log, and the self-assessment in project-docs.
49.tuotos: The collected project journal and AI log in project-docs, a rehearsed 8–10 minute demo, a self-assessment written against the meeting notes, and the handover on Friday 4 December.
49.valmis: Every claim in the documentation has at least one exact reference (commit, test id, note, release); the demo stays inside its time and covers the technique, a bug fix and the Git history; the self-assessment references real meeting notes.
49.label: 30 Nov – 4 Dec
